objects.name: Chipkin Example B-BC
objects.note: the device itself; the instance is configurable with --deviceID. The stack rows are device-wide facts only the stack knows - the protocol version and revision it implements, the services and object types it was configured with, the live object list and address-binding table. The accepted rows are the stack's configured defaults for APDU limits, segmentation, system status and database revision; an application that answered them from its own constants could contradict the stack, so this example does not

objects.name: Bronze
objects.note: REAL, degrees Celsius; starts at 21.5. Also the logged point for Trend Log 1 (Lilac) and one of the three logged points for Trend Log Multiple 1 (Magenta)

objects.name: Emerald
objects.note: starts inactive

objects.name: Hot Pink
objects.note: state 1 of 3: On, Off, Auto

objects.name: Chartreuse
objects.note: commandable; 16-slot Priority_Array, Relinquish_Default 20.0 C, served by GetPropertyReal. Present_Value, Priority_Array and Current_Command_Priority are resolved by the stack from the priority array; also Schedule 1 (Saffron)'s local write target at priority 8, and one of the three logged points for Trend Log Multiple 1 (Magenta). Verified live: a WriteProperty of 42.5 at priority 8 reads back correctly

objects.name: Fuchsia
objects.note: commandable; 16-slot Priority_Array, Relinquish_Default inactive, served by GetPropertyEnumerated

objects.name: Indigo
objects.note: commandable; 16-slot Priority_Array, Relinquish_Default state 1 of 3, served by GetPropertyUnsignedInteger

objects.name: Diamond
objects.note: the humidity this controller READS from peer device 389002's Analog Input 1 (DS-RP-A / DS-RPM-A, main.cpp section 2e) - read-only on the network (a WriteProperty is refused: write-access-denied, Wire Test). Reliability (optional, enabled) says whether the reading is current: no-fault-detected; unreliable-other while the peer flags its own sensor FAULT (the last good value is held); communication-failure before the first reading and whenever the peer has been silent for 3 s (the last good value is kept). The stack derives Status_Flags FAULT from it (cl. 12.4.6). AE-N-I-B: Event_State is NOT a stack default here - it is genuinely computed by the intrinsic OutOfRange algorithm (limits 10..90 percent) this example arms; it is marked accepted only because property-profile-reference.md's generic table does not know an algorithm was armed. Wire Test: peer humidity 95 -> Event_State high-limit, 50 -> normal. Also one of the three logged points for Trend Log Multiple 1 (Magenta)

objects.name: Crimson
objects.note: AE-CRL-B. Priority, Ack_Required and Recipient_List are NOT stack DEFAULTS - they are genuinely populated, by BACnetStack_AddNotificationClassObject (Priority, Ack_Required) and BACnetStack_AddRecipientToNotificationClass (Recipient_List) at start-up. They are marked accepted only because property-profile-reference.md's generic per-type table does not know about this object-specific host-configuration API and so cannot credit them as stack-served. Recipient_List is also registered writable (BACnetStack_SetPropertyWritable) so a client can redirect it at run time; the stack decodes and stores a WriteProperty to it itself. Verified live: Recipient_List reads back the seeded destination. Named Crimson (not Jade, the B-AAC seed's naming defect for this object type - see colour-table.md, Jade is lighting_output's colour) per docs/colour-table.md

objects.name: Vermilion
objects.note: --datalink ipv4 (the default) only: the device has one Network Port, the active data link's (README 'Data links'). BACnet/IP; Network_Type and Protocol_Level are set from BACnetStack_AddNetworkPortObject()'s arguments (IPv4, BACnet Application) at start-up, not a GetProperty callback like the object's other app-served rows; Changes_Pending is likewise computed and answered natively by the stack's Network Port object. Reliability has no fault condition this example detects, so it is accepted at the generic default (normal). Link_Speed is read once at start-up from the host's primary network interface (CASExampleHelper::GetLocalLinkSpeedBitsPerSecond) - 0.0 if the host OS can't report one, which is the spec-correct 'indeterminable' answer, not a bug

objects.name: Cerulean
objects.note: --datalink ipv6 only. BACnet/IPv6 (Network_Type ipv6, 9). IPv6_Address, IPv6_Prefix_Length and IPv6_Default_Gateway are the host interface's (ipv6/LocalIPv6Address.cpp: a global address when the interface has one, else its link-local one), read once at start-up; BACnet_IPv6_UDP_Port is --port. IPv6_DNS_Server is the host's first IPv6 DNS server, one element (the interface's on Windows, /etc/resolv.conf's on POSIX); with none the app declines it and the stack reports one unconfigured entry. The stack serves MAC_Address (the 3-octet VMAC, the device instance) and the multicast address. Link_Speed (optional on this port, so enabled at start-up) as for Network Port 1. Checked with tests/ipv6_probe.py

objects.name: Amber
objects.note: --datalink mstp only. MS/TP (Network_Type mstp, 2). MAC_Address is --mstp-mac (one octet), Link_Speed the baud rate (--mstp-baud; optional on this port, so enabled at start-up), Max_Master and Max_Info_Frames --mstp-max-master / --mstp-max-info-frames - and the stack's MS/TP engine reads its own settings from these same callbacks. Max_Master and Max_Info_Frames are writable as pending changes (Changes_Pending TRUE) that take effect on ReinitializeDevice ACTIVATE_CHANGES. APDU_Length is the stack's 480; the Device's Max_APDU_Length_Accepted reads 480 in this mode

objects.name: Teal
objects.note: --datalink sc only, and only in a build with BACnet/SC (README 'Building with BACnet/SC'). A BACnet/SC node (Network_Type secure-connect, 11) - sc/ScNode.cpp. The stack holds every BACnet/SC property: the hub URIs (--sc-hub, --sc-failover-hub), the 6-octet VMAC, the hub connection status, and the certificate File references (Files 2-5). SC_Primary_Hub_Connection_Status reads connected once the hub has accepted the device

objects.name: Saffron
objects.note: SCHED-E-B. Present_Value, Effective_Period, Schedule_Default, List_Of_Object_Property_References, Priority_For_Writing and Status_Flags are NOT stack DEFAULTS - they are genuinely held and served by the stack's Schedule engine (BACnetStack_AddScheduleObject plus the BACnetStack_SetSchedule*/AddSchedule* configuration calls in main.cpp). List_Of_Object_Property_References has TWO entries (each BACnetStack_AddScheduleObjectPropertyReference call appends): a LOCAL one at Analog Output 1 (Chartreuse) Present_Value, and a REMOTE one at a peer device's (default instance 389002, e.g. a locally-built B-SA-CPP) Analog Output 1 Present_Value - the SCHED-E-B / F-EXTWRITE remote fan-out. Both writes are checked: the local one is inherited from B-AAC's SCHED-I-B, and the remote one is the Wire Test tests/sched_e_b_remote_peer.py. A write made before the peer is bound is kept until it binds (cas-bacnet-stack #2343, fixed at 64b2cfac5; checked by hand). One weekly transition (Monday 08:00) and one exception - a calendar reference to Calendar 1 (Cream), whose Date_List holds December 25 - are seeded at start-up; the 's' key (common/'s DemoAdvance) adds a transition for right now so the change can be observed without waiting for the wall clock

objects.name: Cream
objects.note: stack-held (BACnetStack_AddCalendarObject, cas-bacnet-stack IFC-045 / #1758): the stack stores Date_List (one entry, December 25 of every year, added with BACnetStack_AddCalendarDateEntry) and derives Present_Value from the device's Local_Date. Date_List is WRITABLE (WriteProperty / AddListElement / RemoveListElement) via BACnetStack_SetPropertyWritable. Schedule 1 (Saffron)'s exception is a calendar reference to this object, so any date in Date_List drives Saffron to its exception value

objects.name: Ivory
objects.note: DM-BR-B. A small in-memory STREAM-access file that AtomicReadFile/AtomicWriteFile operate on, and the backup/restore payload for ReinitializeDevice's STARTBACKUP/ENDBACKUP/STARTRESTORE/ENDRESTORE/ABORTRESTORE states (2-6), all accepted by ReinitializeDevice alongside COLDSTART/WARMSTART. BACnetStack_SetBackupAndRestoreEnabled plus the four Prepare/Complete Backup/Restore callbacks are registered. Verified live: File_Size reads 0 (nothing written yet this session) and a WriteProperty of Archive=true reads back correctly

objects.name: Operational Certificate
objects.note: --datalink sc only: a BACnet/SC certificate file in --sc-cert-dir (PEM, File_Type application/x-pem-file; Modification_Date from the file on disk; Archive false). Written with AtomicWriteFile: a new certificate is staged, and ReinitializeDevice ACTIVATE_CHANGES checks it and puts it in place - or refuses it, changing nothing, if it would leave the device unable to connect

objects.name: Lilac
objects.note: T-VMT-I-B / T-ATR-B. Enable, Stop_When_Full, Buffer_Size, Log_Buffer, Record_Count and Logging_Type are NOT stack defaults - they are genuinely held and served by the stack's Trend Log engine (BACnetStack_AddTrendLogObject + SetTrendLogTypeToPolled + SetTrendLogStartStopTime), marked accepted only because property-profile-reference.md's generic table does not know about this host-configuration API. Polls Analog Input 1 (Bronze) Present_Value every second. Log_Buffer is readable only via ReadRange (a plain ReadProperty is rejected with Error(OBJECT, READ_ACCESS_DENIED) - verified live). Record_Count climbs correctly (fixed cas-bacnet-stack#2051 - the Start_Time/Stop_Time window is now built from the same clock, UTC via gmtime, that the stack itself compares against, not local wall-clock) - live-verified: Record_Count climbed from 14 to 44 over 30 seconds. Total_Record_Count (145) is listed in Property_List and climbs with Record_Count (checked by hand at 64b2cfac5; the phase-1 'missing' note read property 322 by mistake - TODO.md). (The #2050 log flood is fixed.)

objects.name: Magenta
objects.note: T-VMT-I-B / T-ATR-B. Enable is NOT a stack default - it is genuinely held and served by the stack's Trend Log Multiple engine (BACnetStack_AddTrendLogMultipleObject + AddLoggedObjectToTrendLogMultiple x3 + SetTrendLogTypeToPolled), marked accepted only because property-profile-reference.md's generic table does not know about this host-configuration API. Polls three points every second: Analog Input 1 (Bronze), Analog Value 1 (Diamond) and Analog Output 1 (Chartreuse) Present_Value. This is the example's working, live-verified polled-logging + ReadRange demonstration: Record_Count climbed from 0 to 150+ across several live runs, and ReadRange (RangeByPosition, first=1, count=5) returned real LogMultipleRecord entries. Total_Record_Count (145) is listed and climbs with Record_Count (checked by hand at 64b2cfac5). (The #2050 log flood is fixed.)
